title: HE WASN’T BETRAYED—HE WAS POSITIONED
paragraphs:
HE WASN’T BETRAYED—HE WAS POSITIONED
The Hidden Hand of God in Joseph’s Pain That Changes How You See Your Own Story Forever
There are moments in life that don’t feel like tests… they feel like betrayal.

Moments where the people who should protect you are the very ones who break you. Moments where the silence of God feels louder than your cries. Moments where you replay everything in your mind asking, “Why would You let this happen to me?”
Joseph knew that feeling.
Not as a theory. Not as a sermon.
As a wound.

The story begins in Genesis 37, but it doesn’t read like a fairytale—it reads like a slow heartbreak. A young man, loved deeply by his father, marked by favor, given dreams straight from God. Dreams so vivid, so prophetic, that even heaven seemed to whisper destiny over his life.
The Hebrew word used when Joseph shares his dream is חֲלוֹם (chalom)—not just a random dream, but a vision infused with divine intention. This wasn’t imagination. This was revelation.
But revelation has a cost.
“And they hated him yet the more for his dreams, and for his words.” (Genesis 37:8)
Hatred grew where love should have lived.
Jealousy began to choke the atmosphere.
And then came the moment that didn’t make sense.
“They took him, and cast him into a pit.” (Genesis 37:24)
The Hebrew word for pit is בּוֹר (bor)—a cistern, empty, dark, abandoned. No water. No escape. No voice hearing you.
Have you ever been there?
Not physically… but spiritually?
Where everything feels stripped. Where what God promised feels buried. Where you're alive—but it feels like something inside you died.
Joseph didn’t just fall into a pit.
He was thrown.
By his own brothers.
By the very people who knew his name.
Then it got worse.
“They sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of silver.” (Genesis 37:28)
Sold.
Not lost.
Not misplaced.
Sold.
For profit.
For convenience.
For silence.

The same kind of silver that would later echo in another betrayal—when Judas handed over Jesus. The Greek word used in the New Testament for betrayal is παραδίδωμι (paradidōmi)—to hand over, to deliver up.
Joseph was handed over.
Jesus was handed over.
And maybe… you feel like you were handed over too.
But here’s where everything changes.
Because what looked like abandonment… was actually orchestration.
Years later, when Joseph finally stands face to face with the very brothers who sold him, he doesn’t speak revenge.
He speaks revelation.
“But as for you, you thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good.” (Genesis 50:20)
The Hebrew phrase here is staggering.

אַתֶּם חֲשַׁבְתֶּם עָלַי רָעָה… אֱלֹהִים חֲשָׁבָהּ לְטֹבָה
“You planned evil against me… God planned it for good.”
The word חָשַׁב (chashav) means to weave, to calculate, to design with intention.
Let that sink in.
God didn’t just “fix” Joseph’s situation.
He designed through it.
The betrayal was real.
The pain was real.
The pit was real.
The slavery was real.
But so was the plan.
And the plan never broke.
Joseph wasn’t sold because God lost control.
Joseph was sold because God was in control.
That’s the part we struggle to accept.
Because we want a God who prevents pain.
But Scripture reveals a God who redeems it.
A God who steps into the very thing meant to destroy you and rewrites it into the thing that positions you.
Joseph thought he was being erased.
But heaven was editing.
Every tear in the pit…
Every step in chains…
Every silent night in a foreign land…
It was all moving him closer—not away—from purpose.
And maybe that’s where this hits you.
Because you’ve been calling it betrayal.
But heaven has been calling it transition.
You’ve been asking “Why me?”
While God has been preparing “Through you.”
Be honest.
This hit harder than you expected.
Someone you know is still stuck in their “pit season.”
Come back to it when doubt creeps in again.
Because it will.
Follow closely, because this is not about motivation—it’s about transformation through Jesus Christ.
And if you’re ready to go deeper—not just emotionally, but spiritually—there’s more waiting for you.
If you truly desire to glorify God with your life, then don’t keep truth to yourself.
Support the mission.
Spread the message.
Let your profile become a place where people encounter Jesus.
Because Joseph’s story wasn’t just about survival.
It was about salvation.
Not just for him… but for many.
And the same God who rewrote his story is still writing yours.
You were never buried.
You were planted.
